## What's new

Threadnote 5.0.4 keeps CLI and MCP graph analysis responsive while it reports exactly how fresh the selected evidence is, helping agents recover predictably when indexing is busy or storage is constrained.

### Bounded analysis and actionable recovery

CLI analysis, reports, and MCP analysis now use an isolated worker with one end-to-end deadline. When indexing is busy, callers receive bounded recovery information instead of waiting behind it. Persisted summaries and paged fallback remain available without a foreground summary write.

### Choose the freshness your task needs

MCP graph analysis now accepts `freshness: current`, `ready`, or `allow-stale`; `current` remains the default and requires a current snapshot. `ready` may use compatible existing evidence, while `allow-stale` never starts indexing. Responses retain the selected policy, snapshot, and scope metadata.

### Safer refresh and capacity handling

Equivalent selected project and worktree scopes share refresh demand while sibling projects remain isolated. Whole-build disk estimates stay advisory, while measured per-write reservations remain enforced and retain capacity evidence for later recovery.
